nodes.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $t$, the acceleration of $r$ at $t$ is the derivative at $t$ of its velocity $s \mapsto r'(s)$, that is $r''(t)$, where a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Acceleration of a space curve

nodes.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with velocity $r'$ and acceleration $r''$, the curvature of $r$ at a real number $t$ is $\kappa(t) = \lVert r'(t) \times r''(t) \rVert / \lVert r'(t) \rVert^3$, where $\times$ is the cross product and $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ is the Euclidean norm; the quotient is $0$ when $r'(t) = 0$.
nodes.title: Curvature of a space curve

nodes.summary: Let $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be a smooth knot, that is, a real-analytic, $2\pi$-periodic curve that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$ and has nonzero velocity everywhere. If the total curvature of $r$ is at most $4\pi$, then $r$ is unknotted: there is a real-analytic isotopy from $r$ to the standard circle through smooth knots.
nodes.title: Fáry–Milnor theorem

nodes.summary: A curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a smooth knot when it is real-analytic, periodic with period $2\pi$, injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, and regular, that is, its velocity $r'(t)$ is nonzero for every real number $t$.
nodes.title: Smooth knot

nodes.summary: A curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is unknotted when there is a real-analytic map $R \colon \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $R(t, 0) = r(t)$ and $R(t, 1) = (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$, the standard circle, for every real number $t$, and for every $s \in [0, 1]$ the curve $t \mapsto R(t, s)$ is a smooth knot.
nodes.title: Unknotted curve

nodes.summary: The period used for parametrised knots is the real number $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Period of a parametrised knot

nodes.summary: Euclidean 3-space is the real vector space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the Euclidean inner product and norm.
nodes.title: Euclidean 3-space for the Fáry–Milnor theorem

nodes.summary: The standard circle is the curve $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$: the unit circle centred at the origin in the $xy$-plane.
nodes.title: Standard circle

nodes.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with velocity $r'$ and curvature $\kappa$, the total curvature of $r$ is the arc-length integral $\int_0^{2\pi} \kappa(t) \, \lVert r'(t) \rVert \, dt$ over one period, where the integral is taken to be $0$ if the integrand is not integrable.
nodes.title: Total curvature of a space curve

nodes.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $t$, the velocity of $r$ at $t$ is its derivative $r'(t)$, taken to be $0$ when $r$ is not differentiable at $t$.
nodes.title: Velocity of a space curve
